gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Powerwall 3 can be added to an existing Powerwall 2 home only as one Powerwall 3 plus up to three Expansion units. Tesla's rules for that pairing are: no more than four Powerwall 2 units, a Backup Gateway 2, Backup Switch or Gateway 3 (Gateway 1, Neurio meters and Powerwall+ are excluded), and Powerwall 3 software 26.26 or later.
standout_why: I compared against EnergySage (cited), itechguides (cited), SolutionEnergy /batteries (cited) and homebatteryreport's DELTA Pro Ultra vs Powerwall 3 page (top result, not cited). On mixing generations, EnergySage, itechguides and SolutionEnergy say nothing about Powerwall 2 and Powerwall 3, or aPower and aPower 2. Homebatteryreport says nothing about Powerwall 2 compatibility, gateways, firmware, or the rule that Expansion units only work on the Leader unit. Homebatteryreport does state the 7-unit maximum (4 Powerwall 3 + 3 Expansion), and EnergySage's 94.5 kWh 'max capacity per inverter' equals 7 × 13.5 kWh. So the system-size cap is partly known, but the rules for adding to Powerwall 2 and the excluded equipment are new.
decides: This confirms Powerwall 3 as 'best overall' for a new install and sharpens the pick for a common shopper: someone who already owns Powerwall 2. Tesla documents adding one Powerwall 3 with up to 3 Expansion units (up to 4 × 13.5 = 54 kWh more) as long as the site has 4 or fewer Powerwall 2 units and an approved gateway. A Powerwall+ or Gateway 1 site has to replace that hardware first, which changes the cost. A FranklinWH aPower 2 buyer should know it scales to 15 units per aGate. I could not read the maker's matrix for mixing it with older aPower units, so I make no claim on that.

findings.label: Maximum system size
findings.value: 7 units: up to 4 Powerwall 3 + up to 3 Expansion units
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Expansion Units (Tesla System Design, en-us)
findings.note: Exact quote: 'The total maximum system size is (7) units - up to (4) Powerwall 3 units with up to (3) Expansion units.' Arithmetic: 7 × 13.5 kWh = 94.5 kWh, which matches EnergySage's figure.

findings.label: Expansion units attach to the Leader only
findings.value: Up to 3 Expansion units on the single Leader Powerwall 3; Expansion units on Follower units 'will not function'
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Expansion Units (Tesla System Design, en-us)
findings.note: The page also says a system can have only 1 Leader, the Expansion Harness is the only approved connection (max combined harness length 4 m / 13 ft when Expansion units connect on one side only), and Expansion units have no inverter.

findings.label: Hardware revision needed for Expansion units
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Expansion Units (Tesla System Design, en-us)
findings.note: Earlier Powerwall 3 part revisions are not listed as compatible with Expansion units.

findings.label: Adding Powerwall 3 to an existing Powerwall 2 site
findings.value: 1 Powerwall 3 + up to 3 Expansion units, added to a site with up to 4 Powerwall 2 units; the Powerwall 3 connects to the last Powerwall 2 in the chain and becomes Site Controller
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Service Manual (en-us): adding Powerwall 3 to a Powerwall 2 system
findings.note: Tesla's own procedure. Sites with more than 4 Powerwall 2 units must replace the extra units with a Powerwall 3 plus Expansion units, or move to a full Powerwall 3 system. Islanding and site metering stay with the existing Backup Gateway 2, Backup Switch or Gateway 3.

findings.label: Exclusions when mixing with Powerwall 2
findings.value: Not supported: Backup Gateway 1 (must be replaced), Neurio meter (replace with Tesla Remote Meter), Powerwall+ (not covered; all Powerwall+ units must be replaced through the Legacy-to-Powerwall 3 upgrade)
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Service Manual (en-us): adding Powerwall 3 to a Powerwall 2 system
findings.note: Backup Switch is allowed only where the local AHJ permits it. Communication cable limit for the whole chain: 150 ft (45 m) at 16 AWG or 82 ft (25 m) at 18 AWG.

findings.label: Firmware needed to commission with Powerwall 2
findings.source_title: Powerwall 3 Service Manual (en-us): adding Powerwall 3 to a Powerwall 2 system
findings.note: Taken from the en-us service manual. Tesla's US and Canada support pages for this returned HTTP 403, so I could not check the consumer-facing wording.

findings.label: Units per aGate
findings.value: Up to 15 aPower 2 per aGate (225 kWh)
findings.source_title: FranklinWH aPower 2 Home Battery Backup (US product page)
findings.note: Same page: 15 kWh, 10 kW continuous, 15-year / 60 MWh warranty, and a footnote that a region-specific version is 'available exclusively in the US & Canada'. Arithmetic: 15 × 15 kWh = 225 kWh.

findings.label: Solar inverter compatibility (maker claim)
findings.value: 'built to be compatible with all solar inverter brands'
findings.source_title: FranklinWH aPower 2: The New Standard for Home Energy Management & Storage (FranklinWH blog, 2025-02-05)
findings.note: This is the maker's own marketing claim, not a tested list. The same post said backward compatibility with earlier aPower was 'anticipated' in 1H2025, so on mixing generations it is out of date.
